_why: The ES7+ React/Redux snippets are the reason most people have that
extension installed: `rfc` writes a component, `useState` writes a
hook, and nobody types either out. These are the same prefixes,
because that is the muscle memory a developer arrives with -- and
the bodies are rustx's, because that is what a .rsx file holds.
A prefix that would write React into a .rsx would be worse than no

A component.description: A component: a function that returns an Element.

A component with props.description: A component whose props are its arguments.

A page.description: A screen under app/. The function is called Page.

State, shared.description: State. At the top of a file it is shared; inside a component it is that instance's own.

An effect.description: Run work when a value changes. The first argument is the dependency.

A value built once.description: keep: built once for the life of this component instance.

A value built once (ref).description: keep, which is also what a ref is here.

Work that waits.description: An async block on the framework's runtime. Network and disk go here.

An input handler.description: onInput, reading the value out of the event.

A keyed list.description: A list. `key` is what carries each item's state when the list reorders.

A condition.description: Either branch is an Element; an empty fragment is the other half.

A fragment.description: Several children with no element around them.

Read this application's own file.description: A file in the folder this system keeps for this application.

Write this application's own file.description: Written whole or not at all.

Check for an update.description: Install the newest release from a GitHub release page.
body: ${2:note} = format!("{} is installed. Restart to use it.", release.version);$0

A context menu.description: The system's own context menu. On Linux, draw one in the page instead.

A native for JavaScript.description: A Rust function a page's JavaScript can call.

A comment.description: A comment inside markup, which is read and discarded.
